recent_articles.title: Lok Sabha election 2024: Maharashtra get interesting after splits in Shiv Sena, NCP - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming Lok Sabha elections in Maharashtra will be influenced by splits within the Shiv Sena and NCP, along with traditional issues like unemployment and farmer suicides. The BJP-Shiv Sena alliance won 41 of the 48 seats in 2019, but the split has shifted the political landscape.  **Eknath Shinde** leads the ruling alliance in Maharashtra, while Ajit Pawar joined the alliance after splitting from the NCP. **Manoj Jarange**, a Maratha quota activist, is gaining traction in Marathwada. The region will be crucial to watch as it has traditionally been a stronghold for the BJP-Shiv Sena.  The elections are scheduled across five phases between April 19 and May 20 with counting on June 4. Over 9.2 crore citizens are eligible to vote, an increase of 34 lakh from 2019.

recent_articles.title: Apple faces Indian engineer’s bias lawsuit - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Apple Inc.** lost an early round in a discrimination lawsuit brought by **Anita Nariani Schulze**, a female engineer from India, who alleges her managers treated her as they would in their own countries.  Santa Clara County Superior Court Judge Sunil R. Kulkarni rejected Apple’s request to dismiss the case, finding that Schulze adequately supported her legal claims. The judge also denied her request to represent a class of female employees who suffered job discrimination over the last four years. Meanwhile, **Cisco Systems Inc.** is facing a suit brought by California's civil rights agency alleging bias against a Dalit employee based on caste.

recent_articles.title: Punjab civic polls: Early edge to Congress as counting proceeds amid tight security - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** is surging ahead in the early stages of counting for **Punjab's** civic body elections, with strong performances in several municipal wards. recent_articles.title: Congress’s message to Siddaramaiah as DKS takes charge: Won’t allow you to rest - Karnataka News | India Today

recent_articles.title: Bengal CID Serves Summons To Abhishek Banerjee In 'Fake Signature' Probe
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **West Bengal CID** served a notice to **Abhishek Banerjee**, TMC national general secretary, requesting his presence for questioning in a probe into alleged forged signatures on a letter supporting **Shobhandeb Chattopadhyay** as the Leader of Opposition. The notice was delivered after officers waited at Banerjee's residence and were directed to his alternative residence before finally serving him the summons.  The CID is investigating discrepancies in the signatures on a May 19 letter submitted by the TMC to the Assembly Secretariat, which some MLAs signed endorsing Chattopadhyay as the LoP. The probe has also questioned several TMC MLAs, including Nayna Banerjee and Kunal Ghosh.

recent_articles.title: Former YSRCP Vinukonda MLA among absconding accused in ₹1,000-crore land scam - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bolla Brahma Naidu**, a former YSRCP MLA from Vinukonda, and his relative **Bolla Ramesh** are key suspects in an alleged ₹1,000-crore government land fraud involving forged government orders (GOs) and the illegal sale of government land in Gandipet.  The case was initiated after a complaint filed by **Gandipet Tahsildar Srinivas Reddy**, alleging that five fabricated GOs were circulated falsely claiming 10 acres of government land had been regularized and allotted to private individuals. The Nimmala family, who have been pursuing legal remedies since 2012, allegedly entered into an agreement with Brahma Naidu and Ramesh to sell the land at ₹3.5 crore per acre.  Police seized bank records, fake MoUs, mobile phones, and a laptop from the arrested accused during their investigation.
